incident-bot: ALERT: High error rate detected for /generate (canary-3). SLO burn starting, paging @sara. https://internal.redwood/alerts/1799991234 :rotating_light:
sara: On it — what's the scope?
sre-oncall: ~10% 5xx from canary-3, latency P95 jumped x3. GPU OOMs on host pool, traffic shift shows new rollout id roll-2026-03-17-09 routed ~15% to canary-3.
alex: That rollout flipped the `staged-latency` feature flag this morning. Should we rollback?
sara: Initiating soft rollback: step 1 reduce canary weight to 0% and observe.
deploy-bot: Commencing traffic update: canary-3 -> 0% (in progress). ETA ~45s.
marco: FYI if we drop weight to 0% we should flush prefix/KV cache on srv-12 to avoid stale routing.
sara: Good call. @marco please run `scripts/flush-prefix.sh srv-12` after drain finishes.
marco: Running now...
marco: OUTPUT: SUCCESS — prefix TTLs cleared on srv-12.
deploy-bot: Traffic update complete — canary-3 at 0%.
sara: Monitoring metrics. Also rolling back artifact to stable tag `prod-1.43.2` across canary pool to be safe.
alex: Are we doing manual rollback or letting auto-rollback handle it? Auto rule threshold is 20% 5xx so it didn't kick.
sara: Manual for now. Also toggling kill-switch: `feature.flag.staged-latency=false` to prevent reflip.
jamie: Customer impact: CS reported 3 customers saw >2x latency, one reported degraded completions but no P0s.
sara: Notifying support & status. @customer-success please post guidance.
customer-success: Drafted status page and emailed affected customers. Created ticket CS-4821 for tracking.
sara: Post-rollback smoke: synthetic /generate requests show P95 back to baseline, 5xxs gone for 2m.
marco: KV cache flush validated, no stale sessions. Infra metrics stabilizing.
sara: Closing active mitigation. Follow-ups: root-cause analysis (alex), threshold tuning (marco), runbook update (jamie). I'll hand off 1hr watch to oncall.
alex: Acknowledged — I'll dig into rollout controller logs and kernel OOM traces.
incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: alerts cleared, monitoring mode. Incident ID INC-2026-179999.
_note: Single-string Slack thread with messages prefixed by sender names. Timestamps are Unix seconds as strings.
